   Green Vernon Commission Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  March 19, 2025
From:  Deborah Harrington, Interim City Clerk
Department:  City Clerk
Submitted by:  Sandra Dolson, City Clerk Specialist

Subject
Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

Recommendation
Select one member to serve as Chair and one member to serve as Vice Chair for the term ending
June 30, 2025.

Background
The Green Vernon Commission consists of seven members including three Vernon Business
Representatives, two Labor Representatives, and two Representatives engaged in the
advancement of Environmental/Sustainability issues. Members serve four-year terms, serving no
more than two full consecutive terms.

The current members are as follows:

Commissioner  Appointing Category  Date Appointed End of Term
Jack Cline  Business Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Ronit Edry  Business Representative  June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Clara Gazcon  Business Representative  June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Catherine Browne Environmental Representative June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Hector Morfin  Environmental Representative June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Martin Perez  Labor Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Stan Stosel  Labor Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028

Section 2.44.050(A) of the Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) requires a Chair and Vice Chair from
different appointing categories. VMC Section 2.44.050(B) prohibits a member from serving as
Chair for more than two (2) consecutive terms. Chair Edry was selected to serve as Chair on
December 12, 2023, serving one (1) term. Commissioner Edry is eligible to serve another term
as Chair if the Commission so determines. Additionally, all other Commissioners are eligible to
serve as Chair.

The Commission should select a Chair and Vice Chair to serve through June 30, 2025.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Meeting Date:  March 19, 2025
From:  Todd Dusenberry, General Manager of Public Utilities
Department:  Public Utilities
Submitted by:  Adriana Ramos, Senior Management Analyst

Subject
Vernon’s Public EV Charging Infrastructure Update

Recommendation
No action required by the Commission. This is an update presentation only.

Background
The City of Vernon (City), along with Vernon Public Utilities (VPU), are committed to doing its
part to help reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, improve local air quality, support zero-
emission electric vehicles (EV) and improve consumer confidence by making EV charging
infrastructure accessible for public use. These efforts are consistent with the City’s Environmental
Sustainability Action Plan (ESAP), strategy T2-a, which outlines the need to expand and maintain
EV charging infrastructure.

The City currently has three public EV charging locations located strategically throughout Vernon
that provide options for workplace, corridor and destination charging. The Soto Charging Plaza
(3805 S. Soto St.) began operations in July 2023, followed by the Alameda Charging Plaza (1850
E. 25th St.) in December 2023. Both sites serve as corridor charging solutions, consisting of 10
publicly accessible Direct Current Fast Chargers (DCFCs) and 8 Tesla Superchargers at each
location, for a total of 36 units combined. In November 2024, VPU also added several public
Level 2 EV charging stations on the rooftop parking lot of Vernon City Hall. Unlike DCFCs, these
Level 2 EV chargers serve as workplace or destination charging solutions for members of the
public visiting City Hall, employees of nearby businesses and City fleet EVs.

VPU’s efforts to promote transportation electrification to its customers and local businesses goes
beyond the development of public EV charging infrastructure. In particular, the utility has robust
incentive programs for electrification, a dedicated EV team to support customers on their
electrification journey, coupled with competitive rates and reliable power. More importantly, VPU
continues to work closely with EV charging infrastructure developers to bring private fleet
charging sites within the City. The developers, who design sites for clients that operate medium
and heavy-duty EVs in the Los Angeles area, are able to take advantage of Vernon’s strategic
location that is in proximity to five major freeways, plus the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
VPU staff will provide a presentation on the City’s public EV charging infrastructure and
incentives for electrification at the Green Vernon Commission meeting on March 19, 2025.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Selection of Chair and Vice Chair
  Recommendation:
  Select one member to serve as Chair and one member to serve as Vice Chair for
  the term ending June 30, 2025.

  Deputy City Clerk Parker presented the staff report.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Perez moved for Commissioner Edry to serve as chair. The motion
  received no second.

  Clarification was provided to the Commission that the municipal code outlines the
  position of Chair as a one-year term and has a two consecutive term limit. Chair
  Edry had served in the position of Chair for two consecutive terms and met the
  threshold for terming out for the Chairperson position.

  Commissioner Browne added she would be willing to serve as Chair for two
  months and re-select Chair Edry the next cycle for another one-year term, which
  would comply with the Code.

  Commissioner Browne moved and Chair Edry seconded a motion to select
  Commissioner Browne to serve as Chair for the term ending June 30, 2025. The
  question was called and the motion carried 5-0, Vice Chair Gazcon and
  Commissioner Morfin absent.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Cline moved and Commissioner Browne seconded a motion to
  select Commissioner Edry to serve as Vice Chair for the term ending June 30,
  2025. The question was called and the motion carried 5-0, Commissioners Gazcon
  and Morfin absent.

  Chairperson Browne moved and received consensus from the Commission for
  Vice Chair Edry to continue to chair the meeting.

  2.  Vernon’s Public EV Charging Infrastructure Update
  Recommendation:
  No action required by the Commission. This is an update presentation only.

  Public Utilities Assistant General Manager Otto presented the staff report and
  Customer Relations and Marketing Manager Sun presented the accompanying
  PowerPoint.
